data.why: The page has a built-in 'Load Example' button and 'Download workbook with examples' buttons that generate example DIGGS/workbook data entirely in JS; no external files are needed to exercise the tool.

goals: Load the built-in example project and see the borings, samples and lab results it contains
Start from a project's DIGGS 3 file and generate a lab workbook listing its borings and samples
Enter soil test results (water content, Atterberg limits, gradation, compaction, etc.) into the workbook and produce a DIGGS XML file with the results attached to the correct borings/samples
Start from a blank workbook (no DIGGS file), enter boring coordinates and test results, and generate a new DIGGS file
Check that a test with raw measurements but no reported result is correctly marked as not reported rather than silently filled in
Re-run an updated workbook against an existing DIGGS file and confirm the earlier results are replaced, not duplicated

review.summary: The tree captures the page's purpose and its two paths well (merge into an existing DIGGS file, or build a new one from typed boring coordinates), with neutral general labels and mostly accurate screens. It leaves out the lab's central step of filling in and re-uploading the workbook, and two of the stated goals (replace-on-rerun, not-reported marking). A few action citations point to the wrong screen, so it needs those fixes before filing.
